To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the data-driven business models of smart cities require a holistic approach to data privacy and security that addresses both technological and social challenges.
the data privacy and security issues in smart cities can be addressed through a holistic view that considers technical, organizational and social aspects.

1) data privacy and security is a major concern for smart cities; 2) the data privacy and security challenges in smart cities can be addressed through a combination of technical measures and strategic organizational decisions; 3) technical solutions for data privacy and security are not enough, and the public has to be involved and educated to understand the benefits of data-driven solutions; and 4) the public has to accept the data-driven solutions to enable the smart city project.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question how to build trust in a smart city by providing privacy-aware data analytics.
a holistic approach to data analytics in smart cities.
the following research questions: How can the privacy and security of citizens be guaranteed in a smart city?

the data analytics in smart city projects is a complex task and needs a careful and well-considered handling of data.
the data privacy and security challenges are not insurmountable, and can be addressed by appropriate technical and organizational measures.
the project is well prepared for the challenges of data analytics and data privacy.

we have shown how a smart city can leverage the benefits of data-driven analytics without compromising privacy.
the smart city project is a great opportunity for data analytics, but it requires a lot of organizational and strategic measures to be able to exploit the full potential of the data.
data analytics is a powerful tool to make the city smarter, but it is also a double-edged sword, which requires careful handling.

the data privacy challenges are not merely technical, but rather organizational.
the data-driven economy is not a zero sum game.
the data privacy and data security measures are crucial to ensure the trust of the public and to guarantee the success of smart cities.
